title: Installed native client audit
summary: Audit of the Interlude-era modified native client corpus: inventory, package formats, read-only tooling, skill/effect and character-appearance evidence, and requirements for client-ready packages.
notes: Manifest-declared type DOC (manifest_override true); classification follows the declared type. Document is a prose-and-tables audit report with evidence pointers, not an ADR (no Status/Decision/Consequences structure), PRD (no user stories or acceptance criteria) or SPEC (no endpoint or schema contract). Owner/dated/work-order statements recorded for synthesizer conflict detection: (1) Section '2026-11-05 source update' (top of doc): 'the current authority is IMPORTA-PC's C:/Lineage2-client' and the E: inventory 'is historical and cannot establish equality without the recorded fleet hash checks'. This dated decision supersedes the E:/lineage2-client inventory as authority. (2) Section 'Requirements for faithful client-ready packages': 'Use this Interlude corpus as its own source profile, with original file/object names, hashes, package versions and dependency closure.' (3) Same section: 'Do not silently combine its skill tables or native meshes with Classic/H5 world assumptions.' (4) Same section: 'Preserve source-relative character/world scale and source animation tracks.' (5) Same section: a drag-and-drop bundle 'must' include geometry/materials, clip names and timing, bone/socket bindings, notification sidecars, audio, effect definitions, skill-to-effect/sound mappings, world transforms and collision metadata in a validated manifest. (6) Section 'Source-backed character appearance': a texture-0 recipe choice or explicit HeadBone attachment 'must remain labeled as a supported preview decision until native runtime behavior is established.' (7) Section 'Source identity': the installation must 'not be described as an untouched official distribution'. (8) Section 'Source-backed character appearance': Greater Musveren resolves to ID 21622, class LineageMonster.field_stalker_20_bi, described as 'client presentation metadata, not authoritative gameplay or full NPC coverage'. No owner decision on which content, race, class or map comes first is stated. Several requirements are normative but are audit findings rather than planning decisions.
